content.title: How to watch the Masters 2026: Round 3 schedule, tee times, Rory McIlroy’s big lead
content.text: Last year, Augusta National stood as Rory McIlroy’s elusive final quest — the daunting omission in his career Grand Slam bid. This year, it looks like his comfort zone.The Masters’ reigning champion is off to an idyllic start at 12 under par. His six-stroke lead through two rounds is a tournament record. McIlroy now tries to become the fourth player ever with back-to-back green jackets. Those chasing his lead include Americans Sam Burns and Patrick Reed, Englishmen Justin Rose and Tommy Fleetwood, and Ireland’s Shane Lowry.Saturday at Augusta means a return to Jim Nantz on the mic. Be among the friends he says hello to with the broadcast info below.All times ET.How to watch the Masters, Round 3 Location: Augusta National Golf Club — Augusta, Ga. Time: 2 p.m., Saturday TV: CBS Streaming: Fubo (Stream Free Now!) CBS is free over the air. All broadcasts and streams are also available on Masters.com and the Masters app.Masters TV format and complete broadcast coverageThe “tradition unlike any other” embraces a new age of TV and streaming. Saturday’s primary coverage is on CBS from 2-7 p.m., with the earlier 12-2 p.m. window airing through Paramount+ and the Masters’ digital destinations.Nantz is the golden, tried-and-true voice of this tournament. This is his 38th year hosting CBS’ Masters coverage. Trevor Immelman, recipient of the green jacket in 2008, is the network’s lead analyst.Your browser does not support the video tag.Now, to the many, many streaming tributaries. Everything below is also on the Masters’ website and app.“On the Range” Time: 10 a.m.-noonCBS Sports Network and Paramount+ air an early live stream from the practice range. Kelly Tilghman is the host, and she’s joined by Michael Breed, Brian Crowell, Amanda Balionis and Iona Stephen.Featured groups Time: 10:15 a.m.-7 p.m.ESPN’s app tracks four groups across the third round. We can safely bet that Group 27 will be included — that’s McIlroy and Burns. The CBS Sports/Paramount+ booth for featured groups is Breed, Crowell, Shane Bacon, Johnson Wagner and Billy Kratzert. Amazon Prime has featured groups, too.Featured holes Time: 10:30 a.m.-6:30 p.m. The ESPN app locks in on holes 4, 5 and 6 starting at 10:30 a.m. ESPN has an additional stream for Nos. 15 and 16, starting at 12:30 p.m. and running up to 6:30 p.m.Elsewhere, Prime Video offers its own stream of the 15th and 16th holes. CBS Sports and Paramount+ do too, with Stephen, Ned Michaels and Geoff Ogilvy as the commentators for that feed.Amen Corner Time: 11:45 a.m.-6 p.m.Prime introduces “Inside Amen Corner,” an alt-cast dedicated to Augusta’s most famous stretch (holes 11-13). “Inside Amen Corner” is hosted by Justin Kutcher; it features Ogilvy and Smylie Kaufman, along with advanced stats and data visualizations.CBS Sports Network and Paramount+ have an Amen Corner outpost, too. That coverage is held down by Grant Boone and Mark Immelman. Never to be outdone, ESPN has cameras fixed on Amen Corner as well.Round 3 tee times for Saturday9:31 a.m. – Kurt Kitayama, Alex Noren 9:42 a.m. – Charl Schwartzel, Rasmus Højgaard 9:53 a.m. – Jon Rahm, Si Woo Kim 10:04 a.m. – Brian Harman, Corey Conners 10:15 a.m. – Sergio Garcia, Maverick McNealy 10:26 a.m. – Keegan Bradley, Viktor Hovland 10:37 a.m. – Justin Thomas, Gary Woodland 10:48 a.m. – Samuel Stevens, Adam Scott 11:10 a.m. – Marco Penge, Matt McCarty 11:21 a.m. – Jordan Spieth, Sepp Straka 11:32 a.m. – Aaron Rai, Jacob Bridgeman 11:43 a.m. – Patrick Cantlay, Sungjae Im 11:54 a.m. – Dustin Johnson, Russell Henley 12:05 p.m. – Harris English, Ryan Gerard 12:16 p.m. – Ludvig Åberg, Scottie Scheffler 12:38 p.m. – Collin Morikawa, Brian Campbell 12:49 p.m. – Nick Taylor, Matt Fitzpatrick 1:00 p.m. – Hideki Matsuyama, Michael Brennan 1:11 p.m. – Jake Knapp, Xander Schauffele 1:22 p.m. – Ben Griffin, Max Homa 1:33 p.m. – Chris Gotterup, Brooks Koepka 1:55 p.m. – Jason Day, Cameron Young 2:06 p.m. – Haotong Li, Kristoffer Reitan 2:17 p.m. – Wyndham Clark, Tyrrell Hatton 2:28 p.m. – Shane Lowry, Tommy Fleetwood 2:39 p.m. – Patrick Reed, Justin Rose 2:50 p.m. – Rory McIlroy, Sam BurnsCurrent Masters standingsMcIlroy is bringing scorching heat to the lush greens. He put up a trim 67 in the opening round, then a Friday-best 65 in the second. Northern Ireland’s superstar has posted 15 birdies thus far, good for 42 percent of his output. For comparison, the tourney field is birdying at a 16 percent clip.The only player to match McIlroy’s 67 on Thursday was Burns, whose best Masters finish is tied for 29th in 2023. He eagled the par-5 second hole for a proper statement, then churned out four birdies to just one bogey. Burns tapered off a bit with a 71 on Friday, but he’s still in the mix for a career moment at 6 under.Reed joins Burns at 6 under after back-to-back 69 scores. Reed eagled twice and had two big sand saves Thursday; he incurred his lone Friday bogey on No. 18. He finished third at last year’s Masters and won it all in 2018.England’s Tyrrell Hatton came closest to McIlroy during the Friday session. He ended the round one stroke shy of the leader at 66. Hatton carried seven birdies and 10 pars before bogeying that pesky last hole, and he went 18-for-18 on greens hit.Rose, who lost to McIlroy in last season’s gripping playoff, is 5 under alongside Fleetwood and Lowry. Rose is a three-time runner-up at Augusta National — the 2025 nail-biter, a playoff loss to Sergio Garcia in 2017 and a second-place tie behind Jordan Spieth in 2015.It’s been a disappointing two days for the sport’s No. 1. Scottie Scheffler sits even through his two rounds. A pair of Friday shots plunked into the water en route to his 2-over 74.Those who missed the weekend cut include Bryson DeChambeau, Bubba Watson and J.J.
